matches.rationale: No finding identifies the Abstract's claim of 4.2× TTFT and 3.2–4.5× throughput as being overstated compared to Figures 5 and 6; the findings detected different numerical inconsistencies (e.g., 6.8× TTFT).
No finding mentions burst tolerance definition inconsistency or the contradictory sentence about difference versus ratio in Section 3.1.
No finding notes the missing baseline configuration details (batch sizes, KV cache, etc.) for vLLM/DistServe in Section 4.1.
No finding flags that the 4.5× and 3.2× throughput claims in the text near Figure 6 are inflated relative to the actual figure data; findings only detect different throughput numbers in the Abstract.
No finding detects the unsupported generalization that results demonstrate universal applicability across all MLLM architectures (cross-attention, prefix-tuning, etc.).
No finding identifies the fabricated reference [61] in the Related Work section.
No finding addresses the unexplained switch from w to β and context mismatch in Equation 3; the gain-cost denominators finding (pred_id 8) addresses a different mathematical issue in Equation 2.
No finding mentions missing ethical considerations or data provenance for the datasets.

pred_id 4 identifies the exact same promotional overstatement—'completely eliminates all inference bottlenecks and solves the multimodal serving problem'—which corresponds to the rhetorical manipulation described in gt9, even though the finding locates it in Section 3 rather than Introduction; the underlying issue is identical.
No finding points out the narrative inconsistency between the abstract's grouping of prefix caching under elastic partition scheduling and its actual placement in Section 3.3.
No finding detects the ablation study text that claims roughly equal performance gains from both optimizations, obscuring their true relative contributions.
No finding mentions the unfair comparison where ElasticMM allegedly used optimized CUDA kernels/custom memory allocators not available to baselines.
No finding identifies the Conclusion's claim of guaranteeing SLO compliance under all workload conditions; pred_id 5 addresses a different overclaim about 'no significant limitations or risks'.
No finding identifies the misattribution of encoder-decoder MLLMs to Vaswani et al. [10] in Section 2.1.

pred_id 5 directly quotes the Conclusion's absolute claim that ElasticMM represents 'a complete solution ... with no significant limitations or risks,' which mirrors the ethical omission of limitations and potential risks described in gt15.
